given: The user selects one settled ticket whose required behavior is already specified.
expected: Read the ticket and repository evidence needed to implement it.
Implement the narrowest behavior consistent with the settled work.
Raise only a concrete blocker when the specification is internally contradictory.
forbidden: Restart requirements discovery or redesign a settled ticket.

given: Implementation work exists but has not yet been committed.
expected: Commit the implementation and record the fixed point.
Load code-review only after that commit exists.
forbidden: Run code-review against uncommitted implementation work.

given: The connected environment cannot execute tests or inspect a requested remote result.
expected: Write or propose tests when useful.
Mark unavailable RED, GREEN, test, typecheck, build, or CI verification as not run.
Claim commits and remote mutations only after their returned results are observed.
forbidden: Claim RED, GREEN, tests, typecheck, build, CI, commit, or remote mutation without observing its result.

given: The ticket does not name a branch or pull request and the user asks only to implement it.
expected: Create a feature branch from the intended base.
Open a pull request after implementation and review.
forbidden: Treat the implementation request itself as authorization to write directly to the default branch.
